## Cats on the Move

Roland Kays et al. (2020) used GPS sensors on pet cats in the US, New Zealand, UK, and Australia to track their movements from 2013 - 2017 to observe their home ranges and potential ecological impacts. Each tracked catʻs characteristics were also noted alongside their GPS movement. Datasets used here are from the Movebank for Animal Tracking Data via Data is Plural.

```{r}
#load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(tidytuesdayR) #cats on the move data
library(maps) #simple polygon basemaps (country, state, county)
library(mapdata)
library(mapproj)

```

```{r}
# Get the Data

# Read in with tidytuesdayR package 
# Install from CRAN via: install.packages("tidytuesdayR")
# This loads the readme and all the datasets for the week of interest

# Either ISO-8601 date or year/week works!

tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load('2023-01-31')

cats_uk <- tuesdata$cats_uk
cats_uk_reference <- tuesdata$cats_uk_reference
```

```{r}
#clean cat data and filter
cleancats <- cats_uk |> 
  filter(visible=="TRUE") |> #to filter out any outliers
  left_join(cats_uk_reference) |> #join datasets together
  group_by(tag_id) |> 
  mutate(totalping=n()) #see which cats got recorded the most, itʻs gracie!
```

```         
```

```{r}
#get UK polygon for the map 
uk <- map_data("world") |> 
  filter(region=="UK")

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cat-move
#| fig-cap: "The small home ranges and large local ecological impacts of pet cats"

#make map of all the cat pings
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data=uk,
               aes(x=long, y=lat, group=group),
                fill="forest green") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.background =
          element_rect(fill = "lightblue")) + #change theme and color of ocean to blue 
  coord_map(projection = "mercator", #this changes the map projection to mercator
            xlim = c(-6, -4), ylim = c(52, 50)) + #change x and y lim to better show data points on the map 
geom_point(data = cleancats,
           aes(x=location_long, y=location_lat, color=animal_sex),  #add in cat data to the polygon
           size = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "yellow")) +
  labs(title = "GPS Tracking Pet Cats in the UK", col="Sex")

ggsave(here("Week_07", "Outputs", "HWmap.png"))
```

Here is a map showing all tracked cat movements, with red points depicting female cats and yellow points depicting male cats. Datasets were cleaned of any outliers prior to mapping. @fig-cat-move
